title: feat(service-record-context): get_record_context lists a long body's outline in pages (outlineFrom / outlineNext)
body:
Fixes #37233

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：外接 AI 读一条正文很长的记录时，目录超过一页上限的部分可以分页继续列出，每个章节都能读到；此前如果几百个标题都在同一层，第 80 个之后的章节 AI 根本读不到。
- 为什么做：记录级 AI 问答专题（资料包读取工具）的后续收尾，补上目录截断后剩余章节无法到达的缺口，并改正一句会误导 AI 的截断提示。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是 AI 读长文时多翻一页或少列几个标题，读到的内容仍受原有长度上限和权限约束；可以直接撤回本次改动。
- 要你做的：无。

## What changes

ADR-0160 D3 "The body"; L1 ACCEPT 7153812992 on PR #37222, nit N2 (this card), N3, N4.

- **The outline comes in pages** (`boundedOutline(headings, from)`, `body-outline.ts`). The pages run through every heading in ONE order — shallowest level first, body order within a level — and a page takes that order from `from` until the next heading would pass either existing bound (80 entries, 8,000 serialized characters); each page lists its headings in body order. Page 1 is today's outline, bar the N3 case below. Every heading is on exactly one page, so following the continuation from page 1 lists every heading with the anchor `headingsOf` gives it. One mechanism serves both cuts: a flat body's pages are runs of it in body order; a nested body's first page is its top levels and later pages carry the deeper headings (which matters too: a top section past the body bound is itself cut, so its sub-headings past the cut were unreachable before as well).
- **Input `outlineFrom`, output `body.outlineNext`** (`record-context-tools.zod.ts`). `outlineNext` is present only when a heading remains that a later page lists; pass it as `outlineFrom`. `outlineFrom` 0 is page 1. An `outlineFrom` past the last page, or on a body that is no outline (carried whole, absent from the pack, withheld from the caller), is ONE answer, `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` 404, as an unresolved `anchor` is. `anchor` with `outlineFrom` is refused `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400 at step 1, before any read.
- **The `outline_truncated` sentence, en and zh-Hans** (`sentences.ts`), now says how many headings this page lists, how many it does not, that pages run shallowest levels first then body order, and the `outlineFrom` that lists the next page (or that no later page lists more). The clause "A listed section's text includes the headings under it" is gone: in a flat cut nothing left out sits under a listed section. The sentence carries numbers only, never an anchor (an anchor is record text, and a note never carries record text) — which is why the cursor is a position and not an anchor.
- **N3, revisited because the paging made it cheap.** A heading whose entry alone passes the character bound fits no page. Without a change it would end the pages (the page that must start with it lists nothing), so the pages now pass over it and the note counts it ("1 heading is too long for any page to list, so its anchor is not given" / "K headings are too long ..."). As a side effect one such heading no longer empties page 1. A body whose ONLY headings are such headings is still carried to the bound and marked truncated, as before. Trade-off stated: such a heading (about 3,950 characters or more of heading text) gets no anchor; in a nested body its text is still inside its parent's section.
- **N4**: no change needed (the changeset it named has merged).
- Tool description: names `outlineNext` / `outlineFrom` beside `anchor`.
- **The `body_outline` note, en and zh-Hans, on every page** now says to read a section with the same objectName, recordId and context, plus the anchor and no `outlineFrom`. Before, it said "the same arguments", and on a page reached through `outlineFrom` those arguments plus an anchor are the pair this PR refuses (review S1).
- The MCP doors needed no code: both pass the input through whole, and the `/mcp` door's registration validates against the spec's `GetRecordContextInputSchema`, so the key is admitted there by the spec change alone. The real-kernel parity cases below prove both doors carry it.

### Design, and the alternative weighed

Continuation (chosen) vs listing every omitted heading's anchor compactly: a compact list is still O(headings) in one answer, so for a large enough body it passes the same bound and needs a cut of its own; the continuation keeps every answer within the existing bounds however big the body, with one mechanism for flat and nested cuts. Cursor: a position in the page order, not an anchor, because the note that tells the model where to continue may not carry record text, and an anchor is derived from heading text.

### Declaration

`Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec` graded `minor` (PM ruling, option A, on this PR's open question): the spec's authorable-surface ledger records `GetRecordContextInput:outlineFrom` and `RecordContextBody:outlineNext` as entered keys, and Check Changeset reads that shard as a metadata-protocol addition (precedent: #37140, #37354). `@objectstack/service-record-context` stays `patch`.

### ADR text this will need (governed, not edited here)

- D4 "Definition", the input line `{ objectName: string, recordId: string, context?: string, anchor?: string }` gains `outlineFrom?: integer` (the output's body gains `outlineNext`).
- D3 "The body", the sentence "A longer body is carried as an outline: its headings in order, each with an `anchor`." needs: an outline past its bounds comes in pages, continued by `outlineFrom`, every heading listed on one page (bar a heading too long to list by itself, stated). Carried by #37490, which should also say that the cursor is a position in the current body, so "exactly one page" holds for one state of the body.

## Tests

See Verification for the commands and readings.

- `body-outline.test.ts`: a flat body of 300 headings pages as 80/80/80/60 and the pages together are exactly the body's headings in order; a nested body's page 1 holds every top heading and later pages only deeper ones, each page in body order, union = all headings, no duplicates; the character bound before the entry cap; an over-long shallowest heading is on no page, counted, and does not empty page 1.
- `record-context-tools.test.ts` (executor): **the acceptance pin** — a body of 300 headings at one level, every page walked by the `outlineNext` the tool gave, all 300 anchors issued once, every section read by its issued anchor and equal to its text, every answer parsing against `GetRecordContextOutputSchema` and within the bounds; the nested cut whose top section is itself cut; the `outline_truncated` sentence for a flat cut AND a nested cut in en AND zh-Hans (counts, `outlineFrom N`, no record text, the old clause absent); the last page; `outlineFrom: 0`; the one 404 answer (past the end / body whole / no body / withheld body); `anchor` + `outlineFrom` refused before any read; negative / fractional / string refused at parse.
- `record-context-tools.zod.test.ts` (spec, new): admits and refuses `outlineFrom` and `outlineNext`, asserting zod's issue code and path; the JSON Schema projection carries `outlineFrom` as an integer of at least 0.
- `mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts` (runtime, real kernel): page 2 over both doors, byte-equal, starts at `clause-(N+1)` (a door that dropped the key would answer page 1), and its anchor reads its section; `outlineFrom` on a body carried whole is the same coded 404 on both doors.
- `mcp-record-context-tools.test.ts`: the registration's input property list gains `outlineFrom`.

## Acceptance notes

- Acceptance bullet 1 (300 same-level headings, every section reached by issued anchors, each answer bounded): pinned in `record-context-tools.test.ts`, "a body of 300 headings at one level".
- Acceptance bullet 2 (the note sentence true for nested and flat cuts, both pinned): "the cut note is true for a flat cut and for a nested cut, in en and zh-Hans".
- Re-reading `outlineFrom` against a body edited between calls simply answers the page at that position of the current body; anchors on it are the current body's, so nothing stale is served.

## Verification

Read first (by risk): `packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts` (`boundedOutline`: the skip of an unlistable heading and where `next` is set), `src/record-context-tools.ts` (the body block: the one 404 for an outline page that does not start where asked), `src/sentences.ts` (`outlineTruncated`).

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-record-context exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/__tests__/record-context-tools.test.ts -t "300 headings"` — one test passes; it walks four pages and reads 300 sections.

All readings at head `5f6f72fd82540c66a716be2a3a874bbd89e58bbd`.

The control, page 2's arguments plus the anchor, is refused `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400.
- Ablation (first round, unchanged code path): `for (let at = from; ...` replaced by `for (let at = 0; ...` in `boundedOutline` turned the 300-heading acceptance pin red (24080 anchors issued, not 300), along with three other executor pins; restored blob equals HEAD.
